title: Simplify stale progress and recovery readiness
summary: Treat stale pipeline progress as quiet historical evidence and automatically retire conclusively dead interrupted lifecycle leases without replaying media work.
reason: Old progress and a dead lifecycle lease were promoted into Review stale progress, Close: active work, and a blocked Launch active-work guard even when no backend process remained alive.
behavior_before: Stale progress rendered as current review work, while an interrupted non-replayable lifecycle lease remained blocked until manual reconciliation and caused close-readiness and Launch preflight to report active work.
behavior_after: Stale progress remains available as raw historical evidence but presents as idle with no stale warning bars. A conclusively dead interrupted lease is written as terminal interrupted evidence, its obsolete lock is removed, no recovery replay occurs, and close-readiness/Launch preflight remain unblocked when all live-work guards are clear.
tests_added: Lifecycle recovery retires unsafe-to-replay interrupted work without invoking replay and preserves terminal evidence.
Close-readiness and Launch preflight stay unblocked after automatic retirement of a conclusively dead lease.
Stale snapshot presentation returns idle/current-work output while retaining raw progress and an explicit stale_evidence health flag.
Launch controller treats stale historical progress as idle unless a separate live/stuck guard is present.
manual_validation: Bundled Python targeted lifecycle, close-readiness, snapshot, and WebView unit suites: 75 tests passed.
Browser-backed Home live-state, Launch/Queue readiness, backend lifecycle, and lifecycle reconciliation smokes: 8 tests passed across four wrappers.
Generated-media adversarial force-kill encode check passed; the partial output was not accepted, the source remained queued, and one temporary partial was retained as evidence.
Generated project index and dependency graph freshness checks passed for the isolated commit candidate.
Targeted Ruff and WebView ESLint completed with no errors; ESLint reported four pre-existing liveRun.js warnings.
Broad release self-test did not pass because the unchanged cross-page static bundle is missing the pre-existing renderPendingRows app-shell token; this is outside the stale-progress/lifecycle scope.
rollback_plan: Revert the listed lifecycle recovery, status presentation, WebView controller/live-run, test, and generated-summary changes. This restores manual lifecycle reconciliation and stale-progress review presentation without touching runtime media or state during rollback.
notes:
Quiet stale progress presentation and automatically retire conclusively dead interrupted leases without replay.
Refreshed generated summaries for files changed by this fix.
Python impact: backend lifecycle recovery and snapshot presentation behavior changed; no contract route, schema file, PowerShell media policy, source mutation, publish, subtitle, audio, or FFmpeg command behavior changed. Real-media validation is not required because media processing policy is unchanged; the required generated-media adversarial force-kill recovery check passed.
Pre-existing edits in lifecycle_lease.py, liveRun.js, and test_application_facade_close_readiness.py were preserved. The worktree contains many additional pre-existing changes that are not part of this packet.
